name: Microsoft for Education Daily
tldr: OneDrive gives every file and folder one link that follows your sharing settings, GitHub and Power Pages get handy previews, and Edge tests a Lockdown Mode.
window: Window: the week's best, from the 80 hours to 06:03 AEDT, Mon 23 Nov 2026 (Thursday 19 to Sunday 22 Nov in the US), plus This-week items.
notes: A thin week for new education-specific news: the week's education stories (Microsoft Classroom, Study and Learn in assignments, Hour of AI, Hwb, Quantum Pioneers) were covered 18-22 Nov, so today's stories are campus-wide updates. This week: OneDrive hero links (Ignite, 17 Nov), Decision-1 as a Foundry judge (18 Nov) and Edge Lockdown Mode (Microsoft's post 13 Nov, press coverage 18-20 Nov).

Status: GitHub's pull request Overview, Power Pages inventory and Decision-1 as a judge are in public preview; Edge Lockdown Mode is an experiment in Edge Canary behind a flag; GPT-6.2 in Microsoft 365 Copilot (from an admin notice) and Windows Server 2028's optional WoW64 (from Windows Central) are as reported; Bungle Brawl's 24 Nov date is subject to change.
Screenshots are the publishers' public pages as captured on 23 Nov 2026; copyright remains with the publishers.

post.text:
IN SAFE HANDS. 🔐

The week's best at Microsoft for education:
- OneDrive: one link per file or folder that updates when you change access
- GitHub's clearer pull request page (preview)
- Power Pages sites in one inventory (preview)
- Edge tests Lockdown Mode

stories.title: OneDrive gives every file and folder one main link
stories.summary: In OneDrive for work or school, every file or folder now has one hero link, shown under File link settings, and Copy link copies it. Change who it works for (only people added, people in your organisation, or anyone, if your IT team allows it) and you don't get a new link: the change applies to everyone who already has it.
stories.for: Teachers, students and staff sharing class work

stories.title: GPT-6.2 Sol is reportedly included with Microsoft 365 Copilot
stories.summary: According to Microsoft's admin notice, as reported by Startup Fortune and Business Upturn, OpenAI's GPT-6.2 Sol ships with the Microsoft 365 Copilot licence, while GPT-6.2 Astra needs usage-based billing and an enabled OpenAI subprocessor setting. Nothing says it reaches student Copilot Chat.

stories.title: GitHub's new pull request page shows more clearly what's blocking a merge
stories.summary: GitHub's new pull request Overview page, in public preview since 5 November, now shows clearer merge status and next steps: failed optional checks no longer make a mergeable pull request look blocked, resolved review threads collapse, and force-pushes link to the old and new commits. You can switch back to the classic view during the preview.

stories.title: Power Pages sites now show up in Power Platform inventory
stories.summary: In public preview, admins can find Power Pages sites in Manage > Inventory in the Power Platform admin center, alongside apps, flows and agents. They can spot sites that allow anonymous access or are owned by people who are leaving, query the inventory through Azure Resource Graph or the Power Platform API, and export it to CSV.

stories.title: Windows Server 2028 reportedly won't run 32-bit apps by default
stories.summary: As reported by Windows Central, the next Windows Server, Windows Server 2028, will make the WoW64 compatibility layer an optional component, so 32-bit apps won't run out of the box. Microsoft's Elden Christensen said 32-bit malware won't be able to run on it. Windows 11 keeps WoW64 by default.

stories.title: Foundry can use Microsoft's Decision-1 model as an evaluation judge
stories.summary: In public preview, Microsoft-Decision-1 can be the judge in Foundry Evaluations, returning a probability for each possible answer instead of a written reason. In Microsoft's tests it took a median of 0.59 seconds and cost $0.12 per 1,000 calls, against $0.70 to $34.39 for 12 chat judges, though it was less accurate than most.
stories.for: University teams testing AI agents for students and staff

stories.title: Microsoft fixed an Entra Connect Health flaw that exposed admin emails and tenant details
stories.summary: Attackers exploited a flaw in the Entra Connect Health API to read admin and technical contact emails and tenant details. Microsoft fixed it on 19 November and notified affected customers through Azure Service Health. No patch is needed, but it advises watching for targeted phishing and using phishing-resistant MFA for privileged accounts.
stories.status: Fixed 19 Nov; no customer action needed

stories.title: Edge is testing a Lockdown Mode for people most at risk
stories.summary: The first version of Edge Lockdown Mode is in Edge Canary behind a flag. It blocks WebGL, WebGL2 and WebGPU on web pages, and Microsoft says today's Canary version would have mitigated roughly 60% of privilege escalation exploits seen in the wild since February 2022. Games, maps and design tools may break, so it isn't meant for everyone.
stories.for: Staff most at risk: IT admins, researchers, leaders
stories.status: Edge Canary experiment, behind a flag

stories.title: Bungle Brawl brings wobbly couch co-op to Xbox on 24 November
stories.summary: Bungle Brawl: Couch Co-op Party is a wobbly physics party brawler for 1 to 4 players on one screen, with bots to fill every match, and costumes like a Banana, a Shark or a Hot Dog. Xbox Wire lists it for 24 November; release dates are subject to change.

transcript.t: This is the Microsoft for Education Daily, for Monday.
Here's what shipped at Microsoft in the last 24 hours.
In safe hands: more of the week's best.
OneDrive now gives every file and folder one main link.
Change who it works for, and that same link updates for everyone.
Teachers, keep a link to the people you added, or open it to everyone at your school.
With Microsoft 365 Copilot, GPT-6.2 Sol is reportedly included.
Coding class? GitHub's new pull request page, in preview, shows more clearly what's blocking a merge.
Failed optional checks no longer make it look blocked, and resolved threads fold away.
Run student portals on Power Pages?
Admins can now find every site in one inventory, in preview.
Spot sites that allow anonymous visitors, or ones owned by staff who are leaving.
For server admins, Windows Server 2028 reportedly won't run 32-bit apps by default.
You can add that back, and Microsoft says 32-bit malware won't run.
Testing a student help agent?
Foundry can now use Microsoft's Decision-1 model as the judge, in preview.
In Microsoft's tests it took under a second, at 12 cents per thousand checks.
The fine print? An Entra Connect Health flaw exposed admin emails and tenant details, and it's now fixed.
No patch is needed, but check Azure Service Health and watch for targeted phishing.
After hours, Edge Canary is testing a Lockdown Mode for people most at risk, like IT admins.
Microsoft says it would have mitigated roughly 60% of real-world privilege escalation exploits.
Plus, Bungle Brawl hits Xbox on the 24th: wobbly brawling for four, on one screen.
One link, a locked-down browser, clear checks: your campus, in safe hands.
Day after day, the updates keep stacking up.
On the release board: shipped, and still shipping.
That was 24 hours at Microsoft. Tomorrow, there's more.
This has been the Microsoft for Education Daily.
Stay curious. See you tomorrow.
